claim: 2D template matching (2DTM) can be used to localize macromolecular complexes in images recorded by cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) with high precision, even in the presence of noise and cellular background.
source: Previously we showed that 2D template matching (2DTM) can be used to localize macromolecular complexes in images recorded by cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) with high precision, even in the presence of noise and cellular background (Lucas et al., 2021; Lucas et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Lucas et al., 2021; Lucas et al., 2022).

claim: Particles localized by 2DTM may be averaged together to generate high-resolution 3D reconstructions.
source: Here, we show that once localized, these particles may be averaged together to generate high-resolution 3D reconstructions.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental results presented in the manuscript.

claim: Regions included in the template may suffer from template bias, leading to inflated resolution estimates and making the interpretation of high-resolution features unreliable.
source: However, regions included in the template may suffer from template bias, leading to inflated resolution estimates and making the interpretation of high-resolution features unreliable.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the methodology and is supported by experimental observations in the manuscript.

claim: A quantitative metric for template bias can aid the interpretation of 3D reconstructions calculated with particles localized using high-resolution templates and fine angular sampling.
source: Moreover, we present a quantitative metric for template bias to aid the interpretation of 3D reconstructions calculated with particles localized using high-resolution templates and fine angular sampling.
evidence: The claim is supported by the development and application of the measure_template_bias program described in the manuscript.

claim: Single-particle cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) has emerged as a high-resolution technique to study molecules and their assemblies in a near-native state over the last decade.
source: Over the last decade, single-particle cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) has emerged as a high-resolution technique to study molecules and their assemblies in a near-native state (Guaita et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Guaita et al., 2022.

claim: In the most favorable cases, cryo-EM can achieve close to 1 Å resolution, rivaling results obtained by protein crystallography.
source: In the most favorable cases, close to 1 Å resolution can be achieved, rivaling results obtained by protein crystallography (Nakane et al., 2020; Yip et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Nakane et al., 2020 and Yip et al., 2020.

claim: Between 20,000 and 70,000 asymmetric units of well-aligned and homogeneous particles have to be averaged to reach sub 2 Å resolution for a high-quality dataset.
source: For a high-quality dataset, between 20,000 and 70,000 asymmetric units of well-aligned and homogeneous particles have to be averaged to reach sub 2 Å resolution (Nakane et al., 2020; Yip et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Nakane et al., 2020 and Yip et al., 2020.

claim: In situ subtomogram averages now approach 3 Å resolution.
source: These in situ subtomogram averages now approach 3 Å resolution (Tegunov et al., 2021), a resolution obtained routinely for single-particle reconstructions in vitro.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Tegunov et al., 2021.

claim: Data collection for tomography requires more time compared to the single-particle technique due to the need for acquiring a tilt series.
source: Data collection for tomography requires more time compared to the single-particle technique due to the need for acquiring a tilt series, and processing tends to be computationally more expensive due to the additional degrees of freedom, compared to 2D images used in the single-particle technique.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about the differences between tomography and single-particle techniques.

claim: Processing for tomography tends to be computationally more expensive due to the additional degrees of freedom, compared to 2D images used in the single-particle technique.
source: Data collection for tomography requires more time compared to the single-particle technique due to the need for acquiring a tilt series, and processing tends to be computationally more expensive due to the additional degrees of freedom, compared to 2D images used in the single-particle technique.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about the computational requirements of tomography versus single-particle techniques.

claim: 2D template matching (2DTM) is an approach that can be used to identify target molecules and complexes in cryo-EM images of cells and cell sections, using single images of nominally untilted specimens.
source: 2D template matching (2DTM) is an approach that can be used to identify target molecules and complexes in cryo-EM images of cells and cell sections, using single images of nominally untilted specimens (Lucas et al., 2022; Lucas et al., 2021; Rickgauer et al., 2020; Rickgauer et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Lucas et al., 2022; Lucas et al., 2021; Rickgauer et al., 2020; Rickgauer et al., 2017.

claim: 2DTM can be used in combination with 3D template matching (3DTM) to identify targets in tomograms collected from the same areas imaged for 2DTM.
source: This approach can be used in combination with 3D template matching (3DTM) to identify targets in tomograms collected from the same areas imaged for 2DTM.
evidence: The claim is based on inference about the complementary use of 2DTM and 3DTM.

claim: 2DTM is fundamentally limited by the background generated by overlapping molecules in untilted views of the sample, imposing a size limit on what can be detected.
source: 2DTM is fundamentally limited by the background generated by overlapping molecules in untiled views of the sample, imposing a size limit on what can be detected (Rickgauer et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Rickgauer et al., 2017.

claim: A combined approach of 2D and 3DTM could benefit from the strengths of both approaches, with better target detection (lower false negative rate) of 3DTM in the tomograms, and the improved overall precision of 2DTM in the untilted views.
source: A combined approach of 2D and 3DTM could benefit from the strengths of both approaches, with better target detection (lower false negative rate) of 3DTM in the tomograms, and the improved overall precision of 2DTM in the untiled views (Lucas et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Lucas et al., 2021 and represents an inference about the complementary benefits.

claim: Targets detected using 2DTM can be used to calculate 3D reconstructions showing novel details not present in the template.
source: In our previous studies, we have demonstrated that the targets detected using 2DTM can be used to calculate 3D reconstructions showing novel details not present in the template (Lucas et al., 2022; Lucas et al., 2021; Rickgauer et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Lucas et al., 2022; Lucas et al., 2021; Rickgauer et al., 2017.

claim: For every detected target, 2DTM determines their x,y location in the image, three Euler angles, and image defocus, that is, all the parameters needed to calculate a single-particle reconstruction.
source: 3D reconstruction is straightforward because for every detected target, 2DTM also determines their x,y location in the image, three Euler angles, and image defocus, that is, all the parameters needed to calculate a single-particle reconstruction.
evidence: The claim is based on the methodology of 2DTM as described in the manuscript.

claim: 2DTM revealed non-modeled density for the viral polymerase (VP1) bound to a rotavirus capsid.
source: Using this approach, we revealed non-modeled density for the viral polymerase (VP1) bound to a rotavirus capsid (Rickgauer et al., 2017), for the small ribosomal subunit (SSU) and tRNAs (Lucas et al., 2022; Lucas et al., 2021), as well as structural differences between Mycoplasma pneumoniae and Bacillus subtilis large ribosomal subunits (LSUs) (Lucas et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Rickgauer et al., 2017.

claim: 2DTM revealed non-modeled density for the small ribosomal subunit (SSU) and tRNAs.
source: Using this approach, we revealed non-modeled density for the viral polymerase (VP1) bound to a rotavirus capsid (Rickgauer et al., 2017), for the small ribosomal subunit (SSU) and tRNAs (Lucas et al., 2022; Lucas et al., 2021), as well as structural differences between Mycoplasma pneumoniae and Bacillus subtilis large ribosomal subunits (LSUs) (Lucas et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Lucas et al., 2022 and Lucas et al., 2021.

claim: 2DTM revealed structural differences between Mycoplasma pneumoniae and Bacillus subtilis large ribosomal subunits (LSUs).
source: Using this approach, we revealed non-modeled density for the viral polymerase (VP1) bound to a rotavirus capsid (Rickgauer et al., 2017), for the small ribosomal subunit (SSU) and tRNAs (Lucas et al., 2022; Lucas et al., 2021), as well as structural differences between Mycoplasma pneumoniae and Bacillus subtilis large ribosomal subunits (LSUs) (Lucas et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Lucas et al., 2021.

claim: Interpretation of reconstructions obtained from 2DTM targets can be hindered by template bias.
source: Interpretation of reconstructions obtained from 2DTM targets can be hindered by template bias (Lucas et al., 2022; Lucas et al., 2021), that is, the reproduction of modeled features included in the template, that are reproduced in the reconstructions, even though they do not correspond to structural features in the detected particles.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Lucas et al., 2022 and Lucas et al., 2021.

claim: Template bias is the reproduction of modeled features included in the template, that are reproduced in the reconstructions, even though they do not correspond to structural features in the detected particles.
source: Interpretation of reconstructions obtained from 2DTM targets can be hindered by template bias (Lucas et al., 2022; Lucas et al., 2021), that is, the reproduction of modeled features included in the template, that are reproduced in the reconstructions, even though they do not correspond to structural features in the detected particles.
evidence: The claim is a definition provided in the manuscript.

claim: Template bias could result from inclusion of pure noise particles and/or local overfitting of particle parameters in the presence of signal.
source: This could result from inclusion of pure noise particles and/or local overfitting of particle parameters in the presence of signal.
evidence: The claim is based on speculation about the causes of template bias.

claim: Previous studies showed that template bias does not prevent the discovery of new structural features at low resolution that were not represented by the template.
source: Our previous studies showed that template bias does not prevent the discovery of new structural features at low resolution that were not represented by the template, but it has yet to be determined if this is true for high-resolution features, which are more susceptible to noise overfitting (Stewart and Grigorieff, 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by inference from previous studies and a citation to Stewart and Grigorieff, 2004.

claim: High-resolution features are more susceptible to noise overfitting.
source: Our previous studies showed that template bias does not prevent the discovery of new structural features at low resolution that were not represented by the template, but it has yet to be determined if this is true for high-resolution features, which are more susceptible to noise overfitting (Stewart and Grigorieff, 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Stewart and Grigorieff, 2004.

claim: 2DTM could in principle be used to study the structure of targets at high resolution, that would otherwise be too small to identify on their own, as long as they bind or are otherwise rigidly attached to a larger target that can be located by 2DTM.
source: 2DTM could in principle be used to study the structure of targets at high resolution, that would otherwise be too small to identify on their own, as long as they bind or are otherwise rigidly attached to a larger target that can be located by 2DTM.
evidence: The claim is based on speculation about the potential applications of 2DTM.

claim: A published single particle dataset of β-galactosidase (Bgal) was analyzed using 2DTM.
source: We analyze a published single particle dataset of β-galactosidase (Bgal) using 2DTM, and 60S LSUs detected in images of Sacchromyces cerevisiae lamellae.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: 60S LSUs were detected in images of Sacchromyces cerevisiae lamellae.
source: We analyze a published single particle dataset of β-galactosidase (Bgal) using 2DTM, and 60S LSUs detected in images of Sacchromyces cerevisiae lamellae.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: High resolution was shown in areas of the reconstruction that were omitted in the template, demonstrating the utility of 2DTM for structure discovery.
source: In both cases, we show high resolution in areas of the reconstruction that were omitted in the template, demonstrating the utility of 2DTM for structure discovery.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: A new metric to quantify template bias in a template-based 3D reconstruction was presented.
source: We present a new metric to quantify template bias in a template-based 3D reconstruction, making reconstruction from 2DTM targets a more broadly useful tool.
evidence: The claim is supported by the development of the measure_template_bias program described in the manuscript.

claim: The published single-particle cryo-EM dataset of Escherichia coli Bgal bound to phenylethyl β-D-thiogalactopyranoside (PETG) was used previously to calculate a 2.2 Å single-particle reconstruction (EMDB-10574).
source: To show the potential of 2DTM to reveal new structural details at high resolution, we analyzed a published single-particle cryo-EM dataset of Escherichia coli Bgal bound to phenylethyl β-D-thiogalactopyranoside (PETG) (Saur et al., 2020). The dataset was used previously to calculate a 2.2 Å single-particle reconstruction (EMDB-10574) that displays density for a number of specifically bound water molecules in the structure, including in the PETG binding pocket.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Saur et al., 2020 and reference to EMDB-10574.

claim: The 2.2 Å single-particle reconstruction (EMDB-10574) displays density for a number of specifically bound water molecules in the structure, including in the PETG binding pocket.
source: The dataset was used previously to calculate a 2.2 Å single-particle reconstruction (EMDB-10574) that displays density for a number of specifically bound water molecules in the structure, including in the PETG binding pocket.
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to EMDB-10574 and citation to Saur et al., 2020.

claim: An atomic model was built into the high-resolution map (PDB: 6TTE).
source: The authors also built an atomic model into the high-resolution map (PDB: 6TTE).
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to PDB: 6TTE.

claim: An atomic model of ligand-free Bgal determined by X-ray crystallography at 1.7 Å (PDB: 1DP0) was used for the template.
source: For our template, however, we used an atomic model of ligand-free Bgal determined by X-ray crystallography at 1.7 Å (PDB: 1DP0) (Juers et al., 2000).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Juers et al., 2000 and reference to PDB: 1DP0.

claim: Using a model that was built into a map that is independent from the data analyzed by 2DTM aids the demonstration of 2DTM as a tool that can make use of atomic models experimentally unrelated to the data being analyzed.
source: Using a model that was built into a map that is independent from the data analyzed by 2DTM aids our demonstration of 2DTM as a tool that can make use of atomic models experimentally unrelated to the data being analyzed.
evidence: The claim is based on inference about the methodological approach.

claim: Atoms in the vicinity of all D2 symmetry-related ligand binding pockets, within a 10 Å radius centered on the side chain amide nitrogen atom of asparagine 102 (in PDB: 1DP0), were removed to demonstrate high resolution in areas omitted in the template.
source: To demonstrate high resolution in areas omitted in the template, we removed atoms in the vicinity of all D2 symmetry-related ligand binding pockets, within a 10 Å radius centered on the side chain amide nitrogen atom of asparagine 102 (in PDB: 1DP0).
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental methodology described in the manuscript.

claim: The truncated atomic model was used to generate a template with cisTEM's simulator.
source: The truncated atomic model was used to generate a template with cisTEM's simulator (Himes and Grigorieff, 2021) (see Materials and methods).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Himes and Grigorieff, 2021 and reference to the Materials and methods section.

claim: 558 micrographs downloaded from the EMPIAR database (EMPIAR-10644) were searched and 59,259 targets with 2DTM SNRs above a threshold of 7.3 were obtained.
source: We searched 558 micrographs downloaded from the EMPIAR database (EMPIAR-10644) and obtained 59,259 targets with 2DTM SNRs above a threshold of 7.3 (Figure 1A), the standard threshold calculated to limit the average number of false positives (false positive rate) to one per micrograph, based on the given search parameters and a Gaussian noise model (Rickgauer et al., 2017) (see Equation 2 below).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and reference to Figure 1A, as well as a citation to Rickgauer et al., 2017.

claim: The standard threshold of 7.3 was calculated to limit the average number of false positives (false positive rate) to one per micrograph, based on the given search parameters and a Gaussian noise model.
source: We searched 558 micrographs downloaded from the EMPIAR database (EMPIAR-10644) and obtained 59,259 targets with 2DTM SNRs above a threshold of 7.3 (Figure 1A), the standard threshold calculated to limit the average number of false positives (false positive rate) to one per micrograph, based on the given search parameters and a Gaussian noise model (Rickgauer et al., 2017) (see Equation 2 below).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Rickgauer et al., 2017 and reference to Equation 2.

claim: Targets were limited to those with 2DTM SNRs above 9.0 to reduce the particles to a number closer to the final dataset used to calculate the 2.2 Å cryo-EM map (49,895), and to enrich for the particles most similar to the template, obtaining a final dataset of 55,627 particles.
source: To reduce the particles to a number closer to the final dataset used to calculate the 2.2 Å cryo-EM map in (49,895), and to enrich for the particles most similar to the template (similar to selecting the best classes in Saur et al., 2020), we limited our targets to those with 2DTM SNRs above 9.0 and obtained a final dataset of 55,627 particles.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental methodology and a citation to Saur et al., 2020.

claim: The identified 55,627 targets were extracted together with their template-matched x,y positions, Euler angles, and CTFFIND4-derived defocus values using prepare_stack_matchtemplate.
source: The identified 55,627 targets were extracted together with their template-matched x,y positions, Euler angles, and CTFFIND4-derived defocus values using prepare_stack_matchtemplate (Lucas et al., 2021), and the particle stack and alignment parameters were imported into cisTEM as a refinement package for further single particle processing.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental methodology and a citation to Lucas et al., 2021.

claim: The Fourier shell correlation (FSC) for the initial reconstruction calculated from the template-matched alignment parameters indicated a resolution of 2.4 Å (FSC = 0.143).
source: The Fourier shell correlation (FSC) (Harauz and van Heel, 1986) for the initial reconstruction calculated from the template-matched alignment parameters indicated a resolution of 2.4 Å (FSC = 0.143) (Rosenthal and Henderson, 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and citations to Harauz and van Heel, 1986 and Rosenthal and Henderson, 2003.

claim: Further refinement against the template while keeping the refinement resolution limit of 3.0 Å – one cycle of defocus and beam tilt refinement, followed by a refinement of alignment parameters and another cycle of defocus and beam tilt parameters – resulted in a final reconstruction with a resolution according to the FSC of 2.2 Å.
source: We performed further refinement against the template while keeping the refinement resolution limit of 3.0 Å – one cycle of defocus and beam tilt refinement, followed by a refinement of alignment parameters and another cycle of defocus and beam tilt parameters. The final reconstruction (Figure 1A–C) displayed a resolution according to the FSC of 2.2 Å (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and reference to Figure 1A–C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Resolution estimates based on the FSC can be affected by template bias.
source: As mentioned above and previously discussed (Lucas et al., 2021), resolution estimates based on the FSC can be affected by template bias.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Lucas et al., 2021.

claim: The resolution estimate of 2.2 Å has to be considered unreliable, and has to be supported by additional evidence, such as inspection of features visible in the density map.
source: Therefore, the present estimate has to be considered unreliable, and has to be supported by additional evidence, such as inspection of features visible in the density map.
evidence: The claim is based on inference about the reliability of resolution estimates in the presence of potential template bias.

claim: Peaks corresponding to detected targets are clearly visible.
source: Peaks corresponding to detected targets are clearly visible (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The average 2DTM SNR for the Bgal dataset was 11.6, and a maximum of 16.3, which is in the range of what is expected for a 465 kDa target.
source: The average 2DTM SNR for this dataset was 11.6, and a maximum of 16.3, which is in the range of what is expected for a 465 kDa target (Rickgauer et al., 2020; Rickgauer et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and citations to Rickgauer et al., 2020 and Rickgauer et al., 2017.

claim: The refined reconstruction shows clear density for PETG and water molecules in the ligand binding pocket that were omitted in the template.
source: The refined reconstruction shows clear density for PETG and water molecules in the ligand binding pocket that were omitted in the template (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and reference to Figure 1C.

claim: Comparison of the 2DTM reconstruction with the published map suggests that they are virtually identical and that there is little or no evidence of template bias in the 2DTM reconstruction.
source: Comparison of this reconstruction with the published map (Figure 1G) suggests that they are virtually identical and that there is little or no evidence of template bias in the 2DTM reconstruction.
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of experimental data and reference to Figure 1G.

claim: An assessment of the local resolution using Phenix indicates a resolution of about 1.8 Å in the binding pocket, consistent with the clear density for water.
source: An assessment of the local resolution using Phenix (Liebschner et al., 2019) further indicates a resolution of about 1.8 Å in the binding pocket, consistent with the clear density for water.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and a citation to Liebschner et al., 2019.

claim: A previously published dataset of 37 images of four FIB-milled lamellae generated from S. cerevisiae cells treated with the translation inhibitor cycloheximide (CHX) to enrich the ribosome population in a single state was used.
source: To investigate whether 2DTM can be used to generate reliable high-resolution reconstructions from images derived from cellular samples, we used a previously published dataset of 37 images of four FIB-milled lamellae generated from S. cerevisiae cells treated with the translation inhibitor cycloheximide (CHX) to enrich the ribosome population in a single state (Figure 2A; Lucas and Grigorieff, 2023).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Lucas and Grigorieff, 2023 and reference to Figure 2A.

claim: The lamella samples were not tilted during data collection and therefore exhibited a small tilt with respect to the electron beam of about 8° due to the milling angle during sample preparation.
source: The lamella samples were not tilted during data collection and therefore exhibited a small tilt with respect to the electron beam of about 8° due to the milling angle during sample preparation.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental methodology described in the manuscript.

claim: 12,210 LSUs were identified with 2DTM in the cytoplasm using a threshold of 7.85 which corresponds to an expectation of one false positive per image across the dataset, or ~0.3% of the particles.
source: We identified 12,210 LSUs with 2DTM in the cytoplasm using a threshold of 7.85 which corresponds to an expectation of one false positive per image across the dataset, or ~0.3% of the particles (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–C.

claim: Local positional and orientational refinement was performed using the cisTEM program refine_template and the original template as a reference.
source: Local positional and orientational refinement was performed using the cisTEM program refine_template (Lucas et al., 2021) and the original template as a reference.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental methodology and a citation to Lucas et al., 2021.

claim: The refined 2DTM coordinates were used to calculate an initial reconstruction with a nominal resolution of 3.15 Å (FSC = 0.143).
source: The refined 2DTM coordinates were used to calculate an initial reconstruction with a nominal resolution of 3.15 Å (FSC = 0.143) (Rosenthal and Henderson, 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and a citation to Rosenthal and Henderson, 2003.

claim: One cycle of beam tilt refinement against the reconstruction improved the resolution to 3.1 Å.
source: One cycle of beam tilt refinement against the reconstruction improved the resolution to 3.1 Å (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and reference to Figure 2A and B.

claim: Further refinement of the other alignment parameters using the reconstruction as a reference caused the resolution to decrease to 8 Å.
source: Unlike for the in vitro Bgal reconstruction, further refinement of the other alignment parameters using the reconstruction as a reference caused the resolution to decrease to 8 Å.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: The reconstruction has reduced signal at high spatial frequencies relative to the template as indicated by the half-map FSC.
source: The reconstruction has reduced signal at high spatial frequencies relative to the template as indicated by the half-map FSC (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The reduced signal at high spatial frequencies, combined with the higher background and lack of low-resolution contrast of the ribosomes in the cellular lamella relative to a purified sample, may reduce the alignment accuracy relative to the high-resolution 2DTM template.
source: This, combined with the higher background and lack of low-resolution contrast of the ribosomes in the cellular lamella relative to a purified sample, may reduce the alignment accuracy relative to the high-resolution 2DTM template.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental observations.

claim: The importance of high spatial frequencies for alignment of particles in images with strong background is highlighted, in contrast to images of purified samples that show strong low-resolution features, which are important for reliable particle alignment.
source: This highlights the importance of high spatial frequencies for alignment of particles in images with strong background, in contrast to images of purified samples that show strong low-resolution features, which are important for reliable particle alignment (Stewart and Grigorieff, 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by inference from the experimental observations and a citation to Stewart and Grigorieff, 2004.

claim: Density consistent with both the 60S (part of the template) and the 40S (outside of the template) was found in the reconstruction of the ribosome from 2DTM coordinates identified in the cytoplasm of FIB-milled S. cerevisiae cell sections.
source: A reconstruction of the ribosome from 2DTM coordinates identified in the cytoplasm of FIB-milled S. cerevisiae cell sections showing clear density for both the 60S (part of the template) and the 40S (outside of the template).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and reference to Figure 2A.

claim: Density consistent with the SSU and tRNAs, that did not derive from the template, was found.
source: As previously reported (Lucas et al., 2022; Lucas et al., 2021), we found density consistent with the SSU and tRNAs, that did not derive from the template.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and citations to Lucas et al., 2022 and Lucas et al., 2021.

claim: Local resolution estimation shows that parts of the SSU are resolved at <4 Å resolution.
source: In the present case, local resolution estimation shows that parts of the SSU are resolved at <4 Å resolution (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and reference to Figure 2B.

claim: The SSU is conformationally variable and shows considerable positional heterogeneity relative to the LSU.
source: The SSU is conformationally variable and shows considerable positional heterogeneity relative to the LSU.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about ribosome structure.

claim: The <4 Å resolution value for parts of the SSU is likely an underestimate of the potential attainable resolution in reconstructions from 2DTM targets in cells.
source: Therefore, this value is likely an underestimate of the potential attainable resolution in reconstructions from 2DTM targets in cells.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the conformational variability and positional heterogeneity of the SSU.

claim: Clear density for tRNAs in the A/A and P/P state with apparent density for the polypeptide on the A site tRNA was observed, and no clear density for E-site tRNAs.
source: Although the map represents an average of all states identified, we observed clear density for tRNAs in the A/A and P/P state with apparent density for the polypeptide on the A site tRNA (Figure 2—figure supplement 2) and no clear density for E-site tRNAs.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: CHX stalls ribosomes in the classical PRE translocation state in vivo, likely by preventing transition of the P/P tRNA to the P/E state consistent with an in vitro structure of the translating Neurospora crassa ribosome and inference from ribosome profiling data.
source: This allowed us to conclude that CHX stalls ribosomes in the classical PRE translocation state in vivo, likely by preventing transition of the P/P tRNA to the P/E state consistent with an in vitro structure of the translating Neurospora crassa ribosome (Shen et al., 2021) and inference from ribosome profiling data (Lareau et al., 2014; Wu et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and citations to Shen et al., 2021, Lareau et al., 2014, and Wu et al., 2019.

claim: The relatively low resolution of the tRNAs likely reflects the mixed pool of tRNA depending on the codons on which the ribosome stalled as well as a mixture of states.
source: The relatively low resolution of the tRNAs likely reflects the mixed pool of tRNA depending on the codons on which the ribosome stalled as well as a mixture of states.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental observations.

claim: Additional density near the ribosomal E site not present in the template was observed that is consistent with the position of CHX in a previously published crystal structure.
source: We observed additional density near the ribosomal E site not present in the template that is consistent with the position of CHX in a previously published crystal structure (Garreau de Loubresse et al., 2014; Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data, a citation to Garreau de Loubresse et al., 2014, and reference to Figure 2C.

claim: The density was sufficiently well resolved to dock CHX and provide in vivo confirmation for the position and orientation of CHX binding in the E site.
source: The density was sufficiently well resolved to dock CHX and provide in vivo confirmation for the position and orientation of CHX binding in the E site.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: Density for eIF5A was not observed but density consistent with binding of spermidine was observed, as has been observed previously for the in vitro CHX-bound N. crassa ribosome (PDB: 7R81).
source: We noted several key differences between the model built from the in vitro CHX-bound structure and the in situ CHX-bound structure. First, we did not observe density for eIF5A but did observe density consistent with binding of spermidine (Figure 2D), as has been observed previously for the in vitro CHX-bound N. crassa ribosome (PDB: 7R81) (Shen et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data, a citation to Shen et al., 2021, and reference to Figure 2D and PDB: 7R81.

claim: Spermidine can bind to ribosomes within cells.
source: This demonstrates that spermidine can bind to ribosomes within cells, however, whether spermidine binds as part of the translation cycle or whether stalling of translation with CHX allowed for spermidine to bind is unclear.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: Whether spermidine binds as part of the translation cycle or whether stalling of translation with CHX allowed for spermidine to bind is unclear.
source: This demonstrates that spermidine can bind to ribosomes within cells, however, whether spermidine binds as part of the translation cycle or whether stalling of translation with CHX allowed for spermidine to bind is unclear.
evidence: The claim is based on speculation about the mechanism of spermidine binding.

claim: Baited reconstruction with 2DTM could be used to further probe the function of polyamides to regulate translation in vivo.
